events.title: France captures Calais, England's last mainland possession
events.description: French troops under the Duke of Guise forced the surrender of Calais, held by England since 1347. Mary I reportedly said that when she died 'Calais' would be found lying in her heart.
events.html: French troops under the Duke of Guise forced the surrender of Calais, held by England since 1347. Mary I reportedly said that when she died 'Calais' would be found lying in her heart.

events.title: Galileo first observes the moons of Jupiter
events.description: Through his improved telescope, Galileo saw small 'stars' beside Jupiter that he soon realised were orbiting it. Bodies circling another planet undermined the belief that everything revolved around Earth.
events.html: Through his improved telescope, Galileo saw small 'stars' beside Jupiter that he soon realised were orbiting it. Bodies circling another planet undermined the belief that everything revolved around Earth.

events.title: Blanchard and Jeffries fly a balloon across the English Channel
events.description: The Frenchman Jean-Pierre Blanchard and the American John Jeffries crossed from Dover to the Forest of Guînes in a hydrogen balloon. They jettisoned almost everything, including clothes, to stay aloft.
events.html: The Frenchman Jean-Pierre Blanchard and the American John Jeffries crossed from Dover to the Forest of Guînes in a hydrogen balloon. They jettisoned almost everything, including clothes, to stay aloft.

events.title: First commercial transatlantic telephone service opens
events.description: A radio-telephone link connected New York and London for paying customers. A three-minute call cost 75 dollars, and transatlantic telephone cables did not arrive until 1956.
events.html: A radio-telephone link connected New York and London for paying customers. A three-minute call cost 75 dollars, and transatlantic telephone cables did not arrive until 1956.

events.title: Truman announces the United States has built a hydrogen bomb
events.description: In his final State of the Union message, Harry Truman disclosed that the US had developed the hydrogen bomb, tested in November 1952. Its power dwarfed the atomic bombs used against Japan.
events.html: In his final State of the Union message, Harry Truman disclosed that the US had developed the hydrogen bomb, tested in November 1952. Its power dwarfed the atomic bombs used against Japan.

events.title: Vietnamese forces capture Phnom Penh and topple the Khmer Rouge
events.description: Vietnam's army took the Cambodian capital, ending Pol Pot's regime, under which some 1.5 to 2 million people had died. A decade of Vietnamese occupation and guerrilla war followed.
events.html: Vietnam's army took the Cambodian capital, ending Pol Pot's regime, under which some 1.5 to 2 million people had died. A decade of Vietnamese occupation and guerrilla war followed.

events.title: Gunmen kill twelve at the Paris offices of Charlie Hebdo
events.description: Two Islamist gunmen attacked the satirical weekly Charlie Hebdo, killing twelve people including leading cartoonists. Millions marched in France days later under the slogan 'Je suis Charlie'.
events.html: Two Islamist gunmen attacked the satirical weekly Charlie Hebdo, killing twelve people including leading cartoonists. Millions marched in France days later under the slogan 'Je suis Charlie'.
